messages:
Sam: Heads-up: following the last RFC about region affinity, i prototyped a lighter-weight client-hint approach for the edge proxy. Instead of changing core routing contracts, client apps can send `X-Region-Preference` + `X-Residency-Consent` and the proxy will prefer local pools but still report explicit routing decisions. Thoughts?
Priya: I like keeping client hints opt-in. Two main concerns: (1) we still need a server-side invariant for 'must not leave residency' tenants; (2) how do we represent multi-constraint cases (eu residency + strict-kms + no-analytics)?
Diego: For (1) we enforce a hard server-side admission check in auth-layer. The proxy may suggest fallbacks, but the authz token includes residency_claims that the router MUST respect. If a request violates residency_claims, reject with 451.
Lena: For (2) propose we compress constraints into a single string tag `residency-policy` with a small grammar, eg: `residency:eu;kms:eu-only;analytics:opt-out`. The router can parse and produce a stable policy id. That keeps headers compact and debuggable.
Sam: Example flow: client includes header, proxy evaluates local capacity -> if saturated consults route-policy-store -> returns RouteSignal to caller with explicit fields in response headers: `X-Route-Region`, `X-Route-PolicyID`, `X-Route-FallbackKind`. This makes the decision observable even if we take fallback.
Priya: Observability is critical. Ops asked for a timeline series per-tenant and per-region: fallback_count, fallback_reason, cost_delta. Also require a label when model fidelity was reduced (we want to know when a request got a smaller model).
Diego: On fidelity reduction: Let's agree on two mechanisms: a) graceful server-side downscaling (same model family but smaller size) b) controlled prompt-trimming + token budget cap. We'll encode which was applied in `X-Route-Fidelity` header (values: `unchanged`, `model-downscale`, `prompt-trim`).
Lena: Backwards compat: not all proxies can parse structured headers. Fallback to `X-Route-Region: eu-west-1` only for old proxies. New routers emit the richer headers.
Sam: Security note: because headers can influence routing, they must be signed by the edge gateway (HMAC) to prevent tampering. infra-bot: policy reminder - all external request hints must be validated and signed.
Priya: About cache coherence: our prefix/KV cache is region-local. If we route to a secondary in-region standby, we need to annotate responses so clients know the cache key remained consistent. Suggest adding `X-Cache-Trust: high|stale|none`.
Diego: Good. Also add a short TTL bump rule when we do a local degrade so downstream caches don't get confused.
Lena: Rollout plan: 1) implement header parsing and policy-id mapping in router service 2) auth-layer residency enforcement 3) emit metrics and response headers 4) canary on internal dev tenants with eu-only constraints 5) docs + SDK hint helper
Sam: Question: should the `route-policy-store` be the source of truth for allowed fallbacks, or should it be computed deterministically from tenant config every time?
Priya: I vote for computed policy from tenant config with a cached policy store for performance. That lets us change policy semantics centrally while still keeping deterministic results for debugging. Cache invalidation events are recorded in audit log.
Diego: Implementation detail: the policy-id can be hash(tenant_id + residency_claims + kms_scope + opt_out_flags). We store the mapping in policy-store for quick lookup but recompute to verify.
Lena: Metrics to add: `route.hint_used`, `route.policy_mismatch`, `fallback.applied`, `fidelity.degraded`. Alert strategy: page on spike in `policy_mismatch` or >0.25% `fidelity.degraded` for strict-residency tenants.
Sam: UX for engineers: small helper lib will surface `shouldSendHint(tenant)` and `serializeResidencyPolicy(...)`. Priya will own the lib.
infra-bot: deploy staged: route-policy-store v0.1 @diego (PR#7012) - canary started :rocket: https://git.internal/r/7012
Sam: Next steps assigned: Priya will open the helper lib PR, Diego will wire policy verification into auth-layer, Lena will update the observability dashboard, i'll coordinate the canary and write the short design note.
Priya: I'll add unit-tests for signed headers and an integration test that simulates a fallback with model-downscale.
Diego: I'll include a simulation harness that replays traffic to measure fidelity-impact and cost-delta.
Lena: I'll add a runbook snippet: if `fidelity.degraded` spikes we revert to strict-region-only routing for affected tenants until we understand root cause.
Sam: Sounds good. If no objections i'll put the minimal header schema in a tiny PR tomorrow and call for review.
Priya: No objections from me. 
Lena: +1
Diego: Go for it.
infra-bot: reminder: compliance check required for egresses to non-eu regions on eu-residency tenants (policy: hard block unless explicit legal waiver).
